title: Mihaly Teleki to Nalaczi, Haller, Apafi, Szepesi, Szalai and Rhedey: 13 letters in number cipher before the 1678 campaign
correspondents: Mihaly Teleki (chancellor of Transylvania) -> Istvan Nalaczi, Janos Haller, Mihaly Apafi, Pal Szepesi, Pal Szalai, Ferenc Rhedey
shelfmark: Teleki Mihaly levelezese VIII (ed. S. Gergely, Budapest 1926) nos. 9, 10, 20, 21, 25, 30, 36, 38, 41, 43, 50, 79, 87 (pp. 9-96); copies from Teleki's chancery letter-book (Lang IDs C.Tel.04, 05, 07, 08, 11, 12, 14, 15, 16, 17, 19, 21, 22)
folio_note: 13 short letters, numbers 1-79 (about 37 distinct values), printed in the edition; Hegedus read C.Tel.15 only (23 Jan 1678)
status: Lang lists all 13 as "megfejtetlen" (numbers, probably homophonic) and the editor did not solve them. Hegedus (NyelvVilag 23, 2020) worked through C.Tel.15 (to Rhedey, 23 Jan 1678) as a monoalphabetic number code and says the key from Teleki's 1666 letter does not fit it: a different clavis was used. The others of Jan-Mar 1678 probably share that clavis. The letter-book is probably DECODE R4819-R4834 (Cluj Reformed diocese; records with no images or decryption; not matched record by record).
why: Transylvania's war council writing in cipher on the eve of the Thokoly/kuruc campaign into Upper Hungary (June 1678).
verify: Obtain Teleki Mihaly levelezese VIII (Arcanum, MEK or a library copy); take the C.Tel.15 key from Hegedus (kripto.blog.hu 2016 and NyelvVilag 23) and run it over C.Tel.04-22; where it fails, solve as monoalphabetic with homophones.

shelfmark: HHStA Wien, Staatenabteilungen, Turkei I, Karton 48, Konv. 3 (1583.04-06), fol. 137-144 and 147-151 (Lang C.Breu.01)
folio_note: about 13 folios, wholly cipher
status: Lang: "megfejtetlen", fully enciphered. Candidate keys on DECODE: R1384 (Breuner 1575, homophonic nomenclator) and R1590 (Chiffrenschluessel, author "Breuner?"); Lang's siblings C.Sin.01-02 (1581) were deciphered at the time.
why: Habsburg ambassador at the Porte in the year of the Habsburg-Ottoman truce renewal; a sister item to the Ungnad and Sinzendorff despatches already tracked.

title: Philipp (Pylyp) Orlyk, Bender: Latin despatches in numeric cipher with the Latin plaintext written between the lines
correspondents: Pylyp Orlyk (hetman in exile of the Zaporozhian Host, Charles XII's circle at Bender) -> a Swedish or allied correspondent ('Excellentia', clear covering letter to Mirowicz at image 43)
shelfmark: Riksarkivet, Diplomatica Muscovitica, Cosacica, SE/RA/2113/2113.2/2 ("Fältherren Philip Orliks brev", 1711-1741), ff. about 38-46 (images 37-42 of R0000481)
folio_note: 394 images (R0000481). Images 37-42: about 6 openings of 2-to-3-digit numbers (values 1-450) with Latin plaintext written line by line above, headed "clavis"; image 43 is the clear covering letter signed Philippus Orlik, Bender 1713.
status: Catalogue calls the volume Orlyk's letters to the Swedish king; no mention of cipher. The images carry an interlinear decipherment in the same hand, so the text was read at the time; no key table seen on these openings (a "clavis" is mentioned in the heading of image 37). Not on DECODE (Nordic dump) and not in the repo.
why: Hetman Orlyk's own cipher during the Pruth aftermath and the Bender stay (Tatar khan, Augustus II, Ukraine, Cossack Ukraine and the Porte): a Ukrainian-Swedish cipher with a plaintext crib for the whole key.
verify: View images 37-43 and 40-42 at full size, transcribe the numerals against the Latin lines, rebuild the key (homophones, nomenclator), then check the rest of the volume for further cipher.

title: Höpken and Carlson (Constantinople) to the Chancery College: four-digit numeric code passages with Swedish interlinear plaintext
correspondents: Carl Fredrik von Höpken and Edvard Carlson -> Kanslikollegium and the chancery president
shelfmark: Riksarkivet, Diplomatica Turcica, SE/RA/2119/2119.1/I/9/22 (Brev till Kanslikollegium och ..., 1734-1737)
folio_note: 695 images (R0003589). Image 383 seen at 1000 px: a Swedish letter with rows of four-digit numbers (1000-1700) and Swedish plaintext written between the rows, underlined. Similar underlined passages at about images 36, 140, 279, 417, 556, 660 (thumbnails).
status: Catalogue: plain letters to the Kanslikollegium and Höpken. The interlinear writing shows the passages were deciphered on receipt; whether every cipher passage in the volume was glossed is not seen. Sibling of the volumes 9/20 and 9/21 (already rows from the 2 Nov volume pass).
why: Ottoman-Swedish diplomacy under Frederick I, with a four-digit word code and a large amount of plaintext crib in one volume.
verify: Page every opening; list the cipher passages and which carry a gloss; build the code from the glossed passages and test it on 9/20-9/21.

title: Gyorgy II Rakoczi, Prince of Transylvania, to Charles X Gustav of Sweden: Latin letters with sign-cipher passages (Polish campaign of 1657)
correspondents: Gyorgy II Rakoczi (Georgius Rakoczy) -> Charles X Gustav, King of Sweden
shelfmark: Riksarkivet, Diplomatica Turcica, bihang Transylvanica, SE/RA/2119/2119.5/4 ("Furstarnas av Siebenbürgen Georg I och II Rácóczis originalbrev till Kungl. Maj:t", 1632-1659), images 18, 20, 22, 23
folio_note: 64 images (R0003533). Images 18 (5 sign lines), 20 (about 6 sign lines in a letter about "Rex Poloniae"), 22 (4 sign lines) and 23 (a full page of about 16 lines of signs, about 500 characters, with a faint Latin gloss between some rows).
status: Catalogue: only "originalbrev" of the two Rakoczi princes; no cipher mentioned. Graphic sign cipher, probably monoalphabetic (the Lang repertory describes the same prince's sign systems in MOL E 190 as "not broken"). A few glosses are written between the rows at image 23, so a partial reading was made at the time. Not in Lang's repertory (checked pp. 191-330 for Swedish-archive items); keys for the same fonds are held (DECODE R4310 "Siebenbürgen Schauis" number key and R4296, Chifferklaver låda II), but they are number keys, not sign keys.
why: Rakoczi's alliance with Charles X Gustav against Poland (Jan 1657): the sign-cipher passages carry the secret terms between the two allies.
verify: View images 18-25 at full size; transcribe the signs, align with the partial glosses on image 23, test as a monoalphabetic sign cipher in Latin; check MOL E 190 sign tables (Lang T.Rag) and the printed Swedish-archive editions of the Rakoczi-Charles X letters.

title: Höpken and Carlson (Constantinople) to the chancery president, 1742: French and Swedish passages in four-digit code with interlinear plaintext
correspondents: Carl Fredrik von Höpken and Edvard Carlson -> the chancery president (Gyllenborg) and the King
shelfmark: Riksarkivet, Diplomatica Turcica, SE/RA/2119/2119.1/I/9/28 (Brev till kanslipresidenten, 1742)
folio_note: 567 images (R0003637). Image 227: a French "extrait de la traduction" of a letter with whole lines of four-digit numbers and French written between them; image 482: a Swedish letter of 22 Sept 1742 with three number blocks glossed in Swedish; underlined interlinear passages also at about 29, 86, 114, 397, 539 (thumbnails).
status: Catalogue: plain letters to the chancery president. Same four-digit code as the sibling volumes 9/20-9/23 and 9/29; glosses written over the numbers show the passages were read on receipt.
why: The last Höpken-Carlson volume (1742, after the Swedish defeat in Finland): the Ottoman side of the Hat government's foreign policy, with plaintext cribs for every passage.
verify: View images 227 and 482 at full size; transcribe, align numerals and glosses, and pool with 9/20-9/23 to rebuild the whole code.
